event: Determine the relative location of a creak and thud sound (door closing) from a robot's perspective.

sounding_object.description: A dark brown wooden arched front door with a small, rectangular, barred window in its upper half. Standard residential door size, approximately 0.9m wide and 2m tall. It is the main entrance door of the house.

reference_object.description: A set of two oval-shaped nested coffee tables. The larger table has a light beige/cream stone-like top and a dark metal frame. The smaller table, also with a similar top and frame, fits partially underneath. Approximate dimensions of larger table: 1m (length) x 0.6m (width) x 0.4m (height).

facing_object.object_name: Light-gray armchair closer to the wall painting
facing_object.description: A light-gray upholstered armchair with a cushioned seat and back, and dark wooden legs. It has a blue patterned decorative pillow. Approximate dimensions: 0.8m (width) x 0.8m (depth) x 0.9m (height). This is the armchair located to the right of the large arched window (when viewed from the room's center) and is closer to a small framed picture on the wall adjacent to a white interior door.

question: Imagine you are a robot standing by a set of nested coffee tables and facing the light-gray armchair closer to the wall painting, when the creak and thud sound comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the sounding object: front-left, front-right, back-left, or back-right? The directions refer to the quadrants of a Cartesian plane (if you are standing at the origin and facing along the positive y-axis). Consider the center point location of the object as the its location.
